messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in kv-cache evictions and token latency observed for route /v1/generate (us-west). Alerts linked: https://internal/observability/alerts/1879995432

kendra: seeing huge rise in unique KV keys/sec (~x43) and continuous-batching small-batch tail latency up. Paging in. Investigating logs now.

mike: I can reproduce in the test replay — sequences that include function calls with structured JSON are producing unique prefixes because the toolcall markers aren't being normalized. lots of cache misses.

sophie: do we have a recent rollout that touched structured_output handling or toolcall prefetching?

andrew: yes, yesterday's routing patch (canary) turned on `structured_output: permissive` by default for the new model variant. that lets tool outputs include free-form JSON headers which change prefixes.

kendra: that matches. continuous batching expects prefix reuse; these new variable function-call tokens blow up the prefix space. KV cache fills with unshared keys, evictions skyrocket, then more misses -> more CPU and latency.

mike: quick proof from prod logs (snip):
```
2026-11-02T15:12:03Z batch_id=bd1 batch_sz=2 route=/v1/generate seq_len=24 toolcall_marker="__func_call_start__{"name":"get_user"...}"
2026-11-02T15:12:03Z kv_put key_hash=0x9f12 len=312
2026-11-02T15:12:04Z kv_put key_hash=0x7b33 len=298
2026-11-02T15:12:04Z kv_evict key_hash=0x3a21
```

sophie: ok we need an emergency mitigation. Options: 1) roll back permissive structured_output flag 2) throttle toolcall-prefetch so toolcalls aren't batched aggressively 3) route traffic to fallback model without toolcall-prefetch.

andrew: I'd prefer throttle + route as fastest. rollback requires a config rollout and might affect other clients. throttling can be pushed locally in the serving layer.

kendra: agree. start with throttling prefetch to 0 for affected route and move 20% traffic to fallback model. prepare rollback if needed.

mike: commands to apply throttling (internal):
```
# throttle toolcall prefetch for route /v1/generate
rwctl route update --route /v1/generate --set toolcall_prefetch=0 --env us-west
# shift 20% traffic to fallback model
rwctl traffic-assign --route /v1/generate --from model:v2 --to model:v1-fallback --percent 20
```

kendra: executing now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rwctl route update --route /v1/generate --set toolcall_prefetch=0 (initiated by kendra)

infra-runbot: canary updated on prod-us-west-1 cluster. 5% -> 20% nodes affected.

mike: monitoring KV evictions and unique-prefix metric: https://internal/observability/dashboards/kv-prefixes

sophie: after throttle, watch for smaller batches but higher micro-latency per token — acceptable short-term tradeoff.

andrew: I'll set a temporary guard in the batching layer to avoid creating batches where first token is a toolcall marker; prefer to flush those requests as singletons to prevent cross-prefix pollution. quick patch, can push as hotfix.

kendra: do that as well. please send the patch command when ready.

andrew: hotfix command (rolling patch):
```
git checkout -b hotfix/kvcache-toolcall
# minimal change: ignore `toolcall_marker` when computing KV prefix hash
apply_patch <<'PATCH'
--- a/runtime/batching/kv_prefix.go
+++ b/runtime/batching/kv_prefix.go
@@
- key := hash(prefix_bytes)
+ // strip in-band toolcall markers before hashing to reduce unique prefix variance
+ normalized := stripToolcallMarkers(prefix_bytes)
+ key := hash(normalized)
PATCH
rwctl deploy --service serving-runtime --image registry/redwood/serving:hotfix-kv-toolfix --rolling --region us-west
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: serving-runtime hotfix-kv-toolfix (initiated by andrew)

kendra: monitoring…

oncall-bot: ALERT update: kv-cache evictions down 78% in 12m after throttle + hotfix canary. tail latency reduced ~40%.

mike: good signal. unique-prefix/sec metric trending down.

sophie: customer impact check: a single large customer reported elevated generation latency and 2 transient 429s at 15:18 UTC. I reached out to SE to confirm.

kendra: noted. I'll assign support to contact effected customers and offer a brief RCA + credit if needed.

mike: leaving a short note for post-incident: structured_output permissive mode caused unnormalized function-call tokens to be included in prefix hash; that created many unique KV prefix keys and caused evictions and batch fragmentation -> latency spike.

andrew: root cause summary: change to default structured handling + missing normalization step in KV prefix computation. Contributing factors: no regression test for function-call prefix variability; no alert for unique-prefix/sec metric threshold.

kendra: action items (short):
- rollback permissive flag if further regressions (owner: product, due: 48h)
- add normalization to prefix computation (owner: runtime, done: in prod hotfix canary)
- add regression test feeding synthetic toolcall-structured outputs (owner: eng-ml, due: 7d)
- add alert: unique-prefix/sec > 10k for 5m (owner: eng-sre, due: 24h)
- customer outreach for reported 429s (owner: support, due: 2h)

sophie: I'll create the support ticket now and ping SE.

kendra: thanks everyone. leaving this thread open until hotfix is fully rolled and support confirms customer contact. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy complete (serving-runtime hotfix-kv-toolfix)

oncall-bot: RESOLVED: alert for kv-cache evictions (incident reduced).

mike: postmortem notes template: https://internal/handbook/incidents/template — I'll start the draft.

andrew: will follow up with a small PR to add a unit test for prefix normalization.

kendra: closing on-page actions and moving to postmortem channel once draft is ready. great work.

support: contacted affected customer at 15:42 UTC, they acknowledged, engineering credit approved.
